h: Getting the most from Priddy's Hard
p: Part of the charm here is the setting itself. Priddy's Hard was a working naval armaments depot for well over two centuries, and walking between the old buildings you get a real feel for how carefully everything had to be laid out. Magazines were kept apart, walls were thick and the whole place was designed around the ever-present risk of a blast. Keep that in mind as you go round and the exhibits start to make a lot more sense.

Allow a couple of hours to take it in properly. Younger children tend to love the sheer size of the guns and the boats, while teenagers and adults often get pulled into the human side of the story, especially the women who filled shells here during the world wars. It's sobering stuff in places, but told in a way that keeps families engaged.
A few tips for a smooth visit:

Check the museum's own website for current opening days, as smaller naval sites often run reduced days outside the main season. Wear comfy shoes, as you'll be on your feet and moving between spaces. Leave a little time for the café and the view across the water, it's a lovely spot to sit and let the history sink in.

Gosport makes a brilliant base for a naval-themed weekend. Stokes Bay is good for a breezy seafront walk, and the Gosport Ferry runs across the harbour to Portsmouth for Gunwharf Quays and the Spinnaker Tower, so you can easily turn one museum visit into a whole weekend by the water.
